title: Animal Imaging
text: Small-animal imaging in mice and rats has become integral to preclinical and translational biomedical research. This non-invasive approach allows for in vivo assessment of biological structures and functions, providing quantitative data on normal and diseased tissues such as tumors, as well as surrounding reactive normal tissues. Its non-invasive nature enables longitudinal studies of rodent models, reducing biological variability and minimizing the number of animals required. These models, expanding exponentially with advances in genetic engineering, offer invaluable insights into the natural history of diseases and treatment responses, which are difficult to replicate in vitro. The Animal Imaging Core offers a comprehensive suite of animal imaging modalities, including MRI, PET, CT, SPECT, and ultrasound, all commonly used in clinical settings, enhancing the likelihood that findings in animal models will be translatable to human patients. Key instruments include 7.0T and 9.4T MRI systems, PET/MR, PET/CT, SPECT/CT, and advanced ultrasound systems, alongside specialized equipment including a small- animal radiation therapy unit and a variety of ancillary tools for advanced imaging analysis. The Core has demonstrated its value supporting at least 900 peer-reviewed publications from 2018-2024 and the acquisition of 11 major instruments funded by NIH and other grants. Supported by a centralized management system, the Core ensures efficient operation, regulatory compliance, and flexible user access. This infrastructure, combined with competitive pricing and integrated support services, establishes the Animal Imaging Core as an essential resource for driving innovation in preclinical cancer research at MSK.

title: An Integrated Analytical Framework for Human Virome Studies: Validation, Standardization, and Statistical Innovation
text:
Viral communities in the human body play critical roles in health and disease, from maintaining immune
homeostasis to driving inflammatory bowel disease, influencing vaccine responses, and affecting susceptibility
to infections including HIV. The Human Virome Program seeks to comprehensively characterize these viral
communities in healthy human cohorts to establish a baseline for comparison to unhealthy/disease virome
states, but current research is hampered by the lack of validated computational tools and statistical methods,
leading to unreliable results and irreproducible findings that impede our understanding of virus-host-
microbiome interactions in human health. This project will create the first integrated benchmarking platform for
virome research, providing validated tools, quality control standards, and statistical best practices that will
ensure HVP studies and the broader virome field can conduct rigorous, reproducible science linking viral
communities to human health outcomes.

title: Prefrontal cortical microcircuit mechanisms for reciprocal interactions between arousal and ethanol consumption
text:
Alcohol use disorders (AUD) exact a major personal, economical, and societal toll, highlighting the urgent need
for developing effective therapeutics. Reciprocal interactions between autonomic arousal and alcohol
consumption play a key role in the etiology of AUD, but the underlying neurobiological mechanisms are poorly
understood. By establishing how top-down modulation of arousal by the prefrontal cortex affects drinking and
how drinking itself modifies top-down control, this proposal will identify novel neural therapeutic targets for
treating excessive drinking driven by aberrant arousal.

title: Unlocking the potential of human hepatocyte plasticity for therapy of cholestatic liver diseases
text:
Diseases of the biliary system are a major indication for liver transplantation, which illustrates the severity of
their impact on patients’ lives and the healthcare system. Studies in mice indicate that hepatocytes can pivot
from their normal function to build a functional biliary system, a therapeutic potential that the proposed project
aims to unlock in humans, particularly in patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis for whom no treatment is
currently available that prevents or delays the need for liver transplantation.

title: Structure and Function of Ionotropic Glutamate Receptors
text:
Ionotropic glutamate receptors (iGluRs) mediate the majority of excitatory neurotransmission in the central
nervous system, while their disfunction is associated with devastating psychiatric, neurological, and
neurodegenerative disorders, including schizophrenia, depression, autism, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis,
epilepsy, and Alzheimer’s disease. We aim to study heteromeric assembly, noncompetitive inhibition, and ion
channel block of AMPA and kainate subtypes of iGluRs using a combination of biophysical and biochemical
approaches. Our results will advance understanding of iGluR structure and function and guide structure-based
drug design.

title: TL1A Regulation of Group 3 Innate Lymphoid Cells in Colitis
text:
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) affects millions of people worldwide and causes significant morbidity. The
objective of this proposal is to identify the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying disease with the long-
term goal of designing targeted therapies that are safer and more effective.

title: Unraveling the pathogenesis of familial dilated cardiomyopathy towards precision medicine
text:
Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a leading cause of heart failure and death, and there is an urgent need to
identify new molecular targets that could lead to the development of more effective treatment strategies. Our
research is focused on a protein called ATF4, which acts as a switch that turns on genes essential for cardiac
muscle function. By studying how ATF4 works, we hope to understand how mutations case DCM and identify
new ways to treat patients.

title: Targeting Dystroglycanopathies using Pluripotent-derived Myogenic Progenitors
text:
This proposal takes advantage of the ability of pluripotent stem cells (PSC) to uniquely produce differentiated
somatic cell types in large quantities. We have developed methods, based on the conditional expression of Pax3
and Pax7, to induce the muscle program in early mesoderm, and thus derive muscle progenitors with great
efficiency for regenerative medicine and disease modeling. Our investigations will focus on understanding the
effect of the environment on the engraftment of PSC-derived myogenic progenitors, and the molecular signature
and long-term regenerative potential of control and gene corrected FKRP mutant PSC-myogenic progenitors.

title: Cell State Network-Directed Therapy
text:
A major contribution to cancer drug resistance is that cancer cells can move into and out of different drug
resistance states. This work aims to build computational models of the timing and probabilities of these events
and how drugs affect them, so that better combination therapies can be designed.

title: The opposing effects of matrix aging and muscle activity on extracellular vesicle promotion of muscle regeneration
text:
A muscle injury often results in persistent functional declines and impaired mobility in older individuals
owing in large part to impaired regenerative responses. With the goal of better understanding the mechanisms
underlying these declines over time, we will: 1) investigate how aging of the skeletal muscle extracellular matrix
(i.e., the scaffolding material that surrounds all cells) alters the ability of extracellular vesicles to promote
functional muscle regeneration, and 2) evaluate whether and how muscle contractile activity reverses these
changes. Our long-term goal is to develop novel therapeutics to enhance tissue healing in a geriatric
population

title: Diabetes Research Center
text:
The Diabetes Research Center at the University of Washington has a long-standing tradition and record of
facilitating scientific investigation aimed at informing on how best to treat and prevent diabetes, obesity, and
related disorders. Through its biomedical research cores, Pilot and Feasibility Program as well as its Enrichment
Program, it will continue to support over 120 scientists in the Greater Seattle area and beyond who are pursuing
basic, translation and clinical investigation in these areas.

title: MRI Core
text: MR Core: Summary/Abstract ADNI MR data has been used extensively in designing Alzheimer’s disease clinical trials, for observational research in normal brain aging and dementia, and for developing new image analysis methods, e.g., machine learning and cognitive/clinical prediction. During ADNI 3, 129 million ADNI MR downloads were provided to users. As in ADNI 2 and 3, the acquisitions for ADNI 4 will be performed at 3T. All sequences will be vendor product and FDA approved for clinical use. The ADNI 4 protocol will include 8 sequences: 3D T1 for morphometry; 3D FLAIR for structural cerebral vascular disease (CVD) ascertainment; a new whole brain sagittal 3D T2 to identify dilated peri vascular spaces; a new 2-tiered T2* gradient recalled echo (GRE) sequence to accommodate standard T2* images as well as the creation of susceptibility weighted imaging (SWI) and quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) at sites that have this capability; a 2-tiered diffusion MRI (dMRI) approach; perfusion arterial spin labeling (ASL) imaging at sites that can acquire 3D ASL; high resolution coronal T2 for hippocampal subfield measures; and task free functional MRI (TF-fMRI). The acquisition time will be under 1 hour to minimize participant burden. The objectives in ADNI 4 will continue to focus on providing curated images and numeric summary values from all MR modalities. ADNI 4 recruitment is anticipated to result in greater pathologic variance, particularly a higher prevalence of CVD. To support this effort, we plan a total of six CVD-related measures in ADNI 4. This includes identification of infarctions, WMH volume, ASL perfusion, diffusion MRI, quantification of dilated peri vascular spaces, and cerebral micro bleeds. Specific aims of the MR core are: Aim 1) Perform data acquisition and quality control and distribute curated images for ADNI users. Aim 2) Provide quantitative measurements for all MR modalities and distribute these for ADNI users. Aim 3) Identify and deploy state of the art methods for post-acquisition data harmonization. While the ADNI core minimizes heterogeneity by standardizing acquisition parameters, some heterogeneity inevitably remains for a variety of reasons. To address this, a major new effort will be added in ADNI 4 to address MR data heterogeneity. Aim 4) Improve participant privacy protection by employing an optimized approach to deface images for each relevant MR modality and distribute defaced images for ADNI users. Aim 5) Optimize prediction of cognitive performance and clinical group membership cross sectionally using imaging and non-imaging data. Aim 6) Optimize predicting future change on functional/psychometric measures and progression from unimpaired to MCI, and MCI to dementia using imaging and non-imaging data. Aim 7) Identify optimum outcome metrics for clinical trials using imaging and non-imaging data.

title: Discovery and Engineering of RiPP Natural Products
text:
Douglas A. Mitchell, Ph.D.
Natural products are highly evolved molecules with useful biological functions and fascinating
chemical structures. These molecules have inspired generations of organic chemists, aided in
the elucidation of fundamental life processes, and served as the most significant source of lead
material for drug discovery. We mine bacterial genomes to discover new natural product
structures and enzyme chemistry with current efforts seeking to engineer the biosynthetic
pathways to produce new-to-nature materials of enhanced biomedical value.

title: Latin American Center for Emerging Infectious Disease Research (LACER)
text:
Our LACER consortium brings together academics, Peruvian government officials, and NGOs with Peru-
and US-based American researchers with established national and international collaborations (> 20
years), including strong regional connections in Ecuador and Brazil, to improve outbreak readiness and
response through rational surveillance strategies for regionally relevant pathogens, across a gradient of
geographical landscapes that reflect the country’s vast ecological diversity. We will 1) Define the geographic
distribution of viral pathogens at the interfaces between human populations and zoonotic transmission
cycles; 2) expand regional viral surveillance strategies tailored to local needs and capacities and improve
local diagnostic assay capabilities and response times, 3) advance characterization of human infection
patterns, phylogeographic relationships, murine and vector infections, and transmission dynamics for
arboviruses (flaviviruses, alphaviruses, and orthobunyaviruses), and 4) define serological impact of
previous viral infection on incursion with other viral species re-emerging and emerging in Latin America.

title: Development of HTS for discovery of IL-25 inhibitors
text:
Specific treatment options against the immune mediator IL-25, which drives inflammatory disease such as
allergic asthma, are currently not available. An important reason for this shortcoming is the complexity of how
IL-25 activates cells, which makes drug discovery difficult. We have devised a new screening approach based
on sophisticated, engineered cell lines and propose in this project to build a drug screening pipeline that can be
used to efficiently identify and develop drugs to ultimately treat IL-25-mediated inflammatory diseases.

title: Syntheses of homogeneous proteoglycan like glycopeptide and glycoprotein libraries for microarray studies
text:
Proteoglycans play important roles in many biological processes such as inflammatory responses,
cancer development, immune modulation, and Alzheimer’s disease. In this project, a new
microarray technology will be developed, which will contain many proteoglycan-like glycopeptides
and glycoproteins bearing homogeneous glycan chains. The availability of this proteoglycan
microarray will enable high-throughput screening of proteoglycan binding, and significantly
advance the better understanding of the fascinating biological functions of proteoglycans.

title: Dissecting the Metabolic Rewiring Mediated by SMARCB1 Loss in Metastatic Bladder Cancer
text:
This proposal aims to define the key metabolic pathways by SMARCB1 loss bladder cancer which support
tumor progression and metastasis. We expect this proposed research will lead to the new targeted pathways
including immunometabolism for bladder cancer patient harboring SMARCB1 loss and serve as a new
metabolic paradigm for the development of personalized therapeutic strategy for bladder cancer.

title: Mechanisms of Nuclear Egress in Gamma-herpesviruses
text:
Kaposi’s sarcoma associated herpesvirus (KSHV) establishes lifelong infections in humans, where it reactivates
and disseminates, causing lymphoproliferative diseases and cancer. Reactivation and dissemination of KSHV
requires production of infectious virions, a process that is dependent on nuclear egress. Given the absence of
virus-specific therapeutics against KSHV, this application proposes to characterize the mechanism of KSHV
nuclear egress with the goal of improving our understanding of herpesvirus biology and identifying potential
therapeutic targets against KSHV and its associated malignancies.

title: Probing functional HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein conformations with novel potent CD4-mimetic compounds
text:
Binding to the CD4 receptor triggers conformational changes in the metastable HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein
trimer that activate its potential to mediate virus entry. CD4-mimetic compounds, small organic molecules that
mimic the CD4 receptor, bind to the envelope glycoprotein trimer and prematurely trigger it, leading to
irreversible inactivation. We describe novel, more potent CD4-mimetic compounds that provide a platform for
further improvement, enable exploration of the basis of susceptibility/resistance among primary HIV-1 strains
and allow better definition of the mechanisms underlying the antiviral potency of CD4-mimetic compounds.

title: Molecular mechanisms that control hematopoietic stem cell lineage bias
text:
Aging and malignancies in humans and mice are linked to disruptions in the epigenetic landscape, leading to
biased hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) differentiation. However, the mechanisms that maintain balanced lineage
output remain unclear. This study will investigate how chromatin remodeling regulates HSC differentiation,
providing insights that could inform novel therapeutic strategies for hematologic disorders.
